correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the triangular difference density w(z)=(1−|z|)+ for differences of independent uniforms and the exact kernel F(a,b). Its second-shift derivative has total mass 2 and deviation ≤2(|a|+b), giving F(a,b)=1/3+a²+b²(log(2/b)−1/2)+O((|a|+b)^3) with appropriate control near z=0. Independently evaluated E[Z²]=1/6 and E[Z² log(1/|Z|)]=7/72. For the interior, Mi=1/3+ℓ²[c²/6+(h²/6)log(2/(hℓ))+h²/72]+O(ℓ³). For boundary classify long-long H=1/3+(ℓ²/2)[c²+h²(log(2/(hℓ))−1/2)], long-short C=1/2+O(ℓ²log(1/ℓ)), and short-short V=1/2+O(ℓ); the exact arclength mixture Mb=(H+2ℓC+ℓ²V)/(1+ℓ)^2 cancels the c² second-order boundary term. This yields Mb=1/3+ℓ/3+ℓ²h²[(1/2)log(2/(hℓ))−3/4]+Oθ(ℓ³log), and subtraction yields the full constant −55h²/72−c²/6. Fresh independent high-precision 1D quadrature of both normalized distance expectations at θ=π/2, π/3, 2.2 and ℓ=.02,.006 gives remainders O(ℓ³ log), with scaled residuals between −0.39 and −0.24. No finite numerical extrapolation was used to prove the fixed-angle theorem.
residual_risks: Remainder constants depend on fixed θ; θ→0 or π is explicitly excluded.
Numerical consistency does not itself bound the analytic remainder uniformly in θ.

value.rationale: The known planar boundary/interior strict inequality has a natural sharpness question on thin convex bodies. The complete fixed-angle first and logarithmic second coefficients classify how the inequality degenerates under a shear and exhibit a nonanalytic angular observable that cannot be read from simple perimeter or area scaling. This is a motivated asymptotic boundary phenomenon with a full finite correction, not a routine restatement of positivity.
residual_risks: Only fixed-angle parallelograms; no uniform angular stability for arbitrary convex sets.

limitations: No claim for θ simultaneously tending to 0 or π with ℓ.
No universally optimal next remainder constant.
